title: Air New Zealand Taps Former Air India CEO Campbell Wilson for Board
excerpt: The New Zealand-born aviation veteran, who led Air India's Tata-era turnaround for nearly four years, joins the national carrier's board as it grapples with aircraft delays and rising fuel costs.
body:
• Air New Zealand will appoint Campbell Wilson and former CFO Robert McDonald to its board effective September 24, 2026.
  • Wilson stepped down as Air India CEO in April 2026 after nearly four years leading the Tata Group-backed turnaround.
  • Air New Zealand faces delayed aircraft deliveries, persistent engine problems, and elevated fuel costs from the Middle East conflict.
  • Wilson brings over 30 years of aviation experience, including founding Singapore Airlines's low-cost carrier Scoot.

Air New Zealand has appointed Campbell Wilson, the former chief executive of Air India, to its board of directors. The airline announced the appointment alongside that of former CFO Robert McDonald, with both set to take their seats effective September 24 at the company's annual shareholders' meeting.

From Air India's Turnaround to Air New Zealand's Boardroom

Wilson, born in Christchurch, New Zealand, brings more than three decades of aviation experience to the role. He served as Air India's CEO and managing director from July 2022, shortly after Tata Group completed its privatization of the airline, until his resignation in April 2026.

His tenure at Air India was marked by an ambitious transformation agenda. Wilson oversaw the merger of Air India with Vistara, the joint venture between Tata Group and Singapore Airlines, consolidating the group's full-service operations. He also managed a massive fleet renewal program and worked to overhaul the airline's service standards.

"It is an honour to be selected to lead the iconic Air India and be a part of the highly respected Tata group."

— Campbell Wilson, at his 2022 appointment as Air India CEO

However, Wilson's final years at Air India were shadowed by persistent losses and intensified regulatory scrutiny following the Air India Flight 171 crash in June 2025, which killed 260 people — the world's deadliest aviation disaster in a decade. Regulators flagged issues ranging from missing emergency equipment checks to maintenance record forgery and crew fatigue management shortcomings.

A Career Built Across Asia-Pacific Aviation

Before Air India, Wilson spent 26 years at Singapore Airlines. He joined as a management trainee in New Zealand in 1996, rising through roles in Canada, Hong Kong, and Japan. In 2011, he became the founding CEO of Scoot, Singapore Airlines' low-cost subsidiary, where he shaped the carrier's informal, irreverent brand identity within a traditionally conservative organization. He later served as Singapore Airlines' Senior Vice President of Sales and Marketing before returning for a second stint leading Scoot in 2020.

Wilson holds a Master of Commerce with First Class Honours from the University of Canterbury.

Air New Zealand's Challenges

The appointments come at a turbulent time for Air New Zealand. The national carrier is navigating delayed aircraft deliveries, persistent engine problems, and elevated fuel costs driven by the ongoing Middle East conflict. McDonald, the other new appointee, currently serves as chair of Contact Energy and as a director at FleetPartners Group, bringing financial and energy sector governance experience to the board.

India-New Zealand Aviation Ties

Wilson's appointment strengthens the aviation bridge between India and New Zealand. His deep operational knowledge of the Indian market — including Air India's route network, partnerships, and the dynamics of one of the world's fastest-growing aviation markets — could inform Air New Zealand's strategy as airlines globally compete for traffic flows through Asia-Pacific. India's outbound travel market has surged in recent years, making it an increasingly important source of passengers for carriers across the region.
